themes.label: AI capital expenditure buildout
themes.rationale: Microsoft is one of the largest hyperscaler capex spenders, building out GPU-dense datacenters for Azure and OpenAI workloads, tying earnings quality to depreciation and capacity utilization trends.

themes.label: Enterprise cloud infrastructure spend
themes.rationale: Azure is a core growth driver funded by enterprise migration and workload expansion; Microsoft's revenue mix is directly exposed to enterprise IT budget cycles and cloud adoption pace.

themes.label: Generative AI product monetization
themes.rationale: Copilot integration across Microsoft 365, GitHub, and Azure AI services represents a major monetization bet on generative AI features, exposing the company to adoption and pricing uncertainty.

themes.label: Power and grid capacity constraints
themes.rationale: Datacenter buildout for AI workloads is increasingly gated by power availability and grid interconnection timelines, directly affecting Microsoft's capacity expansion schedule.

themes.label: Big tech antitrust and regulatory scrutiny
themes.rationale: Microsoft faces ongoing antitrust and regulatory scrutiny in the US and EU over cloud bundling, AI partnerships, and market dominance, posing risk to strategic flexibility.
